children: *Next Raises FY27 Adj Pretax Profit to GBP1.255B From GBP1.24B
Next Nudges Up Guidance After Better-than-Expected Performance
U.K. fashion retailer Next nudged up its guidance for the fiscal year after reporting a rise in earnings in the first half on a better-than-expected performance.

The clothing chain, seen as a bellwether for the U.K. retail sector, said it expected adjusted pretax profit for fiscal 2027 to rise 8.4%  to 1.255 billion pounds ($1.68 billion), citing higher sales expectations and extra cost savings, mostly in warehouse operations. The company had previously guided for 1.24 billion pounds.
Next also raised guidance for international online sales by 40 million pounds, representing a 20.5% jump.

However, expectations for the U.K. are slightly weaker than previously anticipated. Next reduced its sales forecast by 18 million pounds, lowering expected growth to 2.0% from 2.8%. The company said it was concerned about rising inflation, higher mortgage interest costs and a weak employment market.
For the six months through July, Next reported a rise  in pretax profit to 566 million pounds from 509 million pounds in the same period a year earlier.
For the first half of the year, full-price sales--a closely watched industry metric--rose 7.7%, while total group sales rose 9%.
Revenue rose to 3.45 billion pounds from 3.145 billion pounds, beating Visible Alpha consensus of 3.42 billion pounds.
